packet.headline_seed: Logitech’s foldable mouse is for people who refuse to carry a mouse with them
packet.description_seed: I see it often. Hardworking professionals in cafés, airports, or parks hunched over a laptop while carefully dragging their fingers over their PC’s trackpad to navigate some email, project, or alert that can’t be ignored. They would prefer a mouse to a trackpad, but are reluctant to travel with one. When you’re on the go, carrying a mouse can seem burdensome or unnecessary. But I’d argue that it’s worth the boost in efficiency and comfort when navigating your computer, tablet, or phone . For the people who refuse to carry a bulky mouse with them, even when they plan to use their computer away from their desk, I’m glad Logitech launched the Mobi Fold, a foldable, wireless mouse. But I’d still push reluctant mobile mouse users toward something even more comfortable. Logitech’s Mobi Fold The mouse's PAW3222 sensor supports 400-4,000 DPI in 100-DPI increments. Credit: Logitech The Logitech Mobi Fold released today for $80 folds in half so that it’s easy to carry around. Logitech’s announcement claimed that it found that “while 72 percent of professionals own a mouse, only 26 percent actually use one when working in public places.” The announcement didn’t explain Logitech’s methodology, but it seems that someone at the Swiss company has also grimaced at the awkwardly bent wrist of people using laptop trackpads in public. Read full article Comments

I see it often. Hardworking professionals in cafés, airports, or parks hunched over a laptop while carefully dragging their fingers over their PC’s trackpad to navigate some email, project, or alert that can’t be ignored. They would prefer a mouse to a trackpad, but are reluctant to travel with one. When you’re on the go, carrying a mouse can seem burdensome or unnecessary. But I’d argue that it’s worth the boost in efficiency and comfort when navigating your computer, tablet, or phone. For the people who refuse to carry a bulky mouse with them, even when they plan to use their computer away from their desk, I’m glad Logitech launched the Mobi Fold, a foldable, wireless mouse. But I’d still push reluctant mobile mouse users toward something even more comfortable.

The Logitech Mobi Fold released today for $80 folds in half so that it’s easy to carry around. Logitech’s announcement claimed that it found that “while 72 percent of professionals own a mouse, only 26 percent actually use one when working in public places.” The announcement didn’t explain Logitech’s methodology, but it seems that someone at the Swiss company has also grimaced at the awkwardly bent wrist of people using laptop trackpads in public. Logitech’s foldable mouse can get extremely compact, thanks to its distinct hinge, which is encased in accordion-shaped silicone. The hinge pivots at approximately 130 degrees, The Verge reported today.

Logitech is clearly aiming this at people that often work from outside the typical office or home space. The company found that while 72% of professionals own a mouse, only 26% use one while working in public places. The gap, according to Logitech, comes down to bulk and inconvenience. Mobi Fold tries to solve that with a lightweight body, quiet clicks, and a dust-resistant silicone sleeve. It is also rated to withstand 15 years of daily use. Battery life also looks travel-friendly, with just a minute of charging offering up to 22 hours of use, while a full charge lasts up to 30 days.

I see it often. Hardworking professionals in cafés, airports, or parks hunched over a laptop while carefully dragging their fingers over their PC’s trackpad to navigate some email, project, or alert that can’t be ignored. They would prefer a mouse to a trackpad, but are reluctant to travel with one.

When you’re on the go, carrying a mouse can seem burdensome or unnecessary. But I’d argue that it’s worth the boost in efficiency and comfort when navigating your computer, tablet, or phone. For the people who refuse to carry a bulky mouse with them, even when they plan to use their computer away from their desk, I’m glad Logitech launched the Mobi Fold, a foldable, wireless mouse. But I’d still push reluctant mobile mouse users toward something even more comfortable.

The Logitech Mobi Fold released today for $80 folds in half so that it’s easy to carry around. Logitech’s announcement claimed that it found that “while 72 percent of professionals own a mouse, only 26 percent actually use one when working in public places.” The announcement didn’t explain Logitech’s methodology, but it seems that someone at the Swiss company has also grimaced at the awkwardly bent wrist of people using laptop trackpads in public.

Logitech’s foldable mouse can get extremely compact, thanks to its distinct hinge, which is encased in accordion-shaped silicone. The hinge pivots at approximately 130 degrees, The Verge reported today.

Logitech says the Mobi Fold senses when it’s lifted, at which point its buttons will stop working to avoid accidental inputs while you’re folding it. The mouse’s scroll function, which is provided by a touch panel, and tracking will still work during this time.

The Mobi Fold embraces its bendy nature and, sensibly, automatically turns on when opened up and turns off when it’s folded shut. Long battery life is critical to how travel-friendly a mouse is, and this auto-power feature should help users conserve battery, especially compared to traditional wireless mice. It’s easy to forget to flip a wireless mouse’s power switch before putting it in a bag.

[Lähde: Digital Trends]
Laptop trackpads are fine until you get really busy. Editing a spreadsheet in an airport lounge, juggling tabs in a café, or trying to do proper work on a tiny hotel desk can make you miss the convenience of a mouse. Logitech has the answer to this with the new Mobi Fold, its first ultra-portable foldable mouse.

While a small portable mouse is something people carry, many choose to skip the added bulk, simply choosing to bite the bullet with the trackpad. But the Logitech Mobi Fold can simply fold flat, and can later be unfolded when you need to work. This makes it pretty convenient to carry. Logitech even made the mouse to automatically power on when opened and turn off when folded.

Mobi Fold is built around a folding mechanism that turns a pocket-sized accessory into a more traditional mouse shape. Logitech says the design reduces muscle strain by 22% compared to a laptop trackpad, based on its ErgoLab testing. The mouse also has Adaptive Touch Scrolling, which lets users move between precise line-by-line scrolling and faster navigation through longer documents or spreadsheets.

There are also two customizable buttons on the touch panel that can be assigned to shortcuts through the Logi Options+ app. It connects to up to three devices over Bluetooth and supports Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android, iPadOS, and Linux. Logitech is also calling it the company’s first input device to receive Fast Pair certification for quick pairing with compatible Google devices.

Logitech is clearly aiming this at people that often work from outside the typical office or home space. The company found that while 72% of professionals own a mouse, only 26% use one while working in public places. The gap, according to Logitech, comes down to bulk and inconvenience.

Mobi Fold tries to solve that with a lightweight body, quiet clicks, and a dust-resistant silicone sleeve. It is also rated to withstand 15 years of daily use. Battery life also looks travel-friendly, with just a minute of charging offering up to 22 hours of use, while a full charge lasts up to 30 days.

The standard Logitech Mobi Fold is priced at $79.99, $119.99 CAD, €79.99, or £69.99. It comes in Graphite, with Lilac and Off-White available in select markets. There is also Mobi Fold for Business, priced at $89.99, $129.99 CAD, €84.99, or £74.99. That version adds a Logi Bolt USB-C receiver, Sync support for IT monitoring, and a two-year limited hardware warranty.

---

[Lähde: The Next Web]
Logitech has launched the Mobi Fold, its first foldable mouse, aimed at hybrid workers who want a proper mouse on the road but leave it behind because it will not fit in the bag.

The mouse folds to nearly half its size, and the fold is also the power switch: it turns on when opened and off when closed. Logitech says that on-and-off action, plus a small on-device AI model, helps stop accidental clicks as the device is folded away.

Battery is the headline spec. Logitech claims up to 30 days on a full charge, and up to 22 hours from a single minute on the cable. It connects to up to three devices over Bluetooth and works with Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android, iPadOS, and Linux.

The company is pitching the Mobi Fold at what it calls an ‘on-the-go productivity gap’. payload.title: Logitech toi myyntiin taittuvan Mobi Fold -hiiren liikkuvaa työtä varten
payload.summary: Logitechin uusi Mobi Fold on langaton hiiri, joka taittuu kuljetusta varten pienempään kokoon. 80 dollarin laite on suunnattu käyttäjille, jotka työskentelevät usein muualla kuin toimistolla mutta eivät halua kantaa tavallista hiirtä mukanaan.
payload.content:
Logitech on julkaissut Mobi Fold -nimisen langattoman hiiren, jonka keskeinen erikoisuus on taittuva rakenne. 80 dollarin hintainen hiiri on suunnattu etenkin liikkuvaa työtä tekeville käyttäjille, jotka käyttävät kannettavaa tietokonetta kahviloissa, lentoasemilla tai muissa julkisissa tiloissa mutta jättävät erillisen hiiren usein kotiin.

## Taittuva rakenne pienentää kuljetuskokoa

Mobi Fold taittuu puoliksi, jotta se veisi laukussa tai repussa vähemmän tilaa kuin perinteinen hiiri. Sen sarana on suojattu haitarimaisella silikonirakenteella, ja saranan kerrotaan kääntyvän noin 130 astetta. Logitech pyrkii tuotteella ratkaisemaan ongelmaa, jossa hiiri koetaan hyödylliseksi mutta liian kömpelöksi ottaa mukaan lyhyisiin työhetkiin kodin tai toimiston ulkopuolella.

Hiiren PAW3222-anturi tukee 400–4 000 DPI:n herkkyyttä 100 DPI:n välein. Lisäksi laitteessa on kevyt runko, hiljaiset napsautukset ja pölyä hylkivä silikonisuoja. Näillä ominaisuuksilla Mobi Foldia asemoidaan matkakäyttöön tilanteissa, joissa käyttäjä haluaa välttää pelkkään kosketuslevyyn nojaamisen mutta ei halua kuljettaa täysikokoista hiirtä.

## Logitech hakee ratkaisua julkisten tilojen työskentelyyn

Logitechin mukaan 72 prosentilla ammattilaisista on hiiri, mutta vain 26 prosenttia käyttää sellaista työskennellessään julkisissa paikoissa. Yhtiön mukaan ero johtuu erityisesti hiiren koosta ja mukana kuljettamisen vaivasta. Näiden lukujen taustalla olevaa tutkimusmenetelmää ei kuitenkaan ole avattu lähdeaineistossa, joten niitä kannattaa pitää Logitechin omana markkinointiväitteenä.

Akkukeston osalta Mobi Fold on suunniteltu nopeisiin lähtöihin. Yhden minuutin latauksen kerrotaan riittävän enintään 22 tunnin käyttöön, ja täyden latauksen luvataan kestävän jopa 30 päivää. Hiiren kerrotaan myös kestävän 15 vuoden päivittäistä käyttöä.

## Pieni koko vastaan käyttömukavuus

Mobi Foldin kiinnostavuus riippuu lopulta siitä, painottaako käyttäjä mahdollisimman pientä kuljetuskokoa vai pidempien työrupeamien ergonomiaa. Taittuva rakenne tekee siitä tavallista matkahiirtä helpommin mukana kulkevan vaihtoehdon, mutta mukavuudessa se joutuu silti kilpailemaan suurempien kannettavien hiirten kanssa.

There is also Mobi Fold for Business, priced at $89.99, $129.99 CAD, €84.99, or £74.99. That version adds a Logi Bolt USB-C receiver, Sync support for IT monitoring, and a two-year limited hardware warranty.

Logitech has launched the Mobi Fold, its first foldable mouse, aimed at hybrid workers who want a proper mouse on the road but leave it behind because it will not fit in the bag.

The mouse folds to nearly half its size, and the fold is also the power switch: it turns on when opened and off when closed. Logitech says that on-and-off action, plus a small on-device AI model, helps stop accidental clicks as the device is folded away.

Battery is the headline spec. Logitech claims up to 30 days on a full charge, and up to 22 hours from a single minute on the cable. It connects to up to three devices over Bluetooth and works with Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, Android, iPadOS, and Linux.

article.content:
Logitech on julkaissut Mobi Fold -nimisen langattoman hiiren, jonka keskeinen erikoisuus on taittuva rakenne. 80 dollarin hintainen hiiri on suunnattu etenkin liikkuvaa työtä tekeville käyttäjille, jotka käyttävät kannettavaa tietokonetta kahviloissa, lentoasemilla tai muissa julkisissa tiloissa mutta jättävät erillisen hiiren usein kotiin.

## Taittuva rakenne pienentää kuljetuskokoa

Mobi Fold taittuu puoliksi, jotta se veisi laukussa tai repussa vähemmän tilaa kuin perinteinen hiiri. Sen sarana on suojattu haitarimaisella silikonirakenteella, ja saranan kerrotaan kääntyvän noin 130 astetta. Logitech pyrkii tuotteella ratkaisemaan ongelmaa, jossa hiiri koetaan hyödylliseksi mutta liian kömpelöksi ottaa mukaan lyhyisiin työhetkiin kodin tai toimiston ulkopuolella.

Hiiren PAW3222-anturi tukee 400–4 000 DPI:n herkkyyttä 100 DPI:n välein. Lisäksi laitteessa on kevyt runko, hiljaiset napsautukset ja pölyä hylkivä silikonisuoja. Näillä ominaisuuksilla Mobi Foldia asemoidaan matkakäyttöön tilanteissa, joissa käyttäjä haluaa välttää pelkkään kosketuslevyyn nojaamisen mutta ei halua kuljettaa täysikokoista hiirtä.

## Logitech hakee ratkaisua julkisten tilojen työskentelyyn

Logitechin mukaan 72 prosentilla ammattilaisista on hiiri, mutta vain 26 prosenttia käyttää sellaista työskennellessään julkisissa paikoissa. Yhtiön mukaan ero johtuu erityisesti hiiren koosta ja mukana kuljettamisen vaivasta. Näiden lukujen taustalla olevaa tutkimusmenetelmää ei kuitenkaan ole avattu lähdeaineistossa, joten niitä kannattaa pitää Logitechin omana markkinointiväitteenä.

Akkukeston osalta Mobi Fold on suunniteltu nopeisiin lähtöihin. Yhden minuutin latauksen kerrotaan riittävän enintään 22 tunnin käyttöön, ja täyden latauksen luvataan kestävän jopa 30 päivää. Hiiren kerrotaan myös kestävän 15 vuoden päivittäistä käyttöä.

## Pieni koko vastaan käyttömukavuus

Mobi Foldin kiinnostavuus riippuu lopulta siitä, painottaako käyttäjä mahdollisimman pientä kuljetuskokoa vai pidempien työrupeamien ergonomiaa. Taittuva rakenne tekee siitä tavallista matkahiirtä helpommin mukana kulkevan vaihtoehdon, mutta mukavuudessa se joutuu silti kilpailemaan suurempien kannettavien hiirten kanssa.

I see it often. Hardworking professionals in cafés, airports, or parks hunched over a laptop while carefully dragging their fingers over their PC’s trackpad to navigate some email, project, or alert that can’t be ignored. They would prefer a mouse to a trackpad, but are reluctant to travel with one. When you’re on the go, carrying a mouse can seem burdensome or unnecessary. But I’d argue that it’s worth the boost in efficiency and comfort when navigating your computer, tablet, or phone. For the people who refuse to carry a bulky mouse with them, even when they plan to use their computer away from their desk, I’m glad Logitech launched the Mobi Fold, a foldable, wireless mouse. But I’d still push reluctant mobile mouse users toward something even more comfortable.

The Logitech Mobi Fold released today for $80 folds in half so that it’s easy to carry around. Logitech’s announcement claimed that it found that “while 72 percent of professionals own a mouse, only 26 percent actually use one when working in public places.” The announcement didn’t explain Logitech’s methodology, but it seems that someone at the Swiss company has also grimaced at the awkwardly bent wrist of people using laptop trackpads in public. Logitech’s foldable mouse can get extremely compact, thanks to its distinct hinge, which is encased in accordion-shaped silicone. The hinge pivots at approximately 130 degrees, The Verge reported today.

Logitech is clearly aiming this at people that often work from outside the typical office or home space. The company found that while 72% of professionals own a mouse, only 26% use one while working in public places. The gap, according to Logitech, comes down to bulk and inconvenience. Mobi Fold tries to solve that with a lightweight body, quiet clicks, and a dust-resistant silicone sleeve. It is also rated to withstand 15 years of daily use. Battery life also looks travel-friendly, with just a minute of charging offering up to 22 hours of use, while a full charge lasts up to 30 days.
